subject: use inla.make.lincombs() in a spatio-temporal model

messages.author: 05197463d4d8b3b0
messages.subject: use inla.make.lincombs() in a spatio-temporal model
parts:
Hi, I have an enquiry about the new feature inla.make.lincombs()
If my model is a spatio-temporal model   GF + AR(1), which is specified as 
formula <- (ncatch ~ 1  + LongCenter + LatCenter + 
                    f(field, model = spde, group=time, control.group=list(model="ar1")))

I can get the joint marginals for the intercept, and the covariates for longitude&latitude, but how to deal with the GF+AR(1) part? 
Given that I need to project the latent field from the mesh to the grid, in this case I am not sure how to include both the fixed effects and the random effects in inla.make.lincombs()?

Cheers, 
Joyce

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] use inla.make.lincombs() in a spatio-temporal model
parts:
The easiest solutions to this is if you already use inla.stack and an
"A-matrix"; then you can skip using lincombs and do the posterior
lincombs using a prediction stack.

Alternatively, you can construct a prediction matrix (A-matrix) using
inla.spde.make.A (which supports space-time models via "group", just
as in your f-function call) for the space-time part of the model and
use that as input to inla.make.lincombs.

/Finn
